# Realtime Robotics Names Kevin Carlin Chief Executive Officer to Lead Company’s Next Phase of Growth

August 13, 2026

#### Co-founder Peter Howard to Serve as Chairman as Realtime Robotics Builds on Momentum With Key Customers in Automotive Manufacturing

BOSTON – August 13, 2026 – Realtime Robotics, the leader in industrial AI for automated robot system design and deployment, today announced that Kevin Carlin has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. Carlin succeeds Co-founder Peter Howard, who continues as non-executive Chairman of the Board. [...] About Realtime Robotics  
 Realtime Robotics is the leader in industrial AI for automated robot system design and deployment. The company helps the world’s largest manufacturers plan, launch, and run production lines with greater speed, confidence, and flexibility, turning what was once a slow, high-risk process into a fast, predictable path from concept to production. That means faster product launches, fewer costly surprises on the factory floor, and the agility to adapt as market demands change. For more information, please visit our website and follow us on LinkedIn.

Realtime Robotics has appointed Kevin Carlin as Chief Executive Officer, succeeding co-founder Peter Howard, who will continue with the industrial AI company as non-executive Chairman of the Board.

Carlin’s appointment is effective immediately and comes as Realtime Robotics looks to capitalize on growing adoption of its Resolver platform among global automotive manufacturers.

Carlin joined Realtime Robotics in 2022 as Chief Commercial Officer and was promoted to President and Chief Commercial Officer in 2025. He has more than two decades of international leadership experience spanning semiconductors, industrial automation and artificial intelligence. [...] Before joining Realtime Robotics, Carlin spent more than 13 years at Analog Devices. His roles there included senior leadership positions within the Automation & Energy Group and Industrial Automation business. He also built an internal startup focused on AI- and machine learning-powered sensing and analytics.

“Kevin has been instrumental in building the customer relationships and commercial engine behind that success,” Howard said. “He has the experience and the instincts to drive the company from this inflection point into rapid growth.”

As CEO, Carlin plans to deepen Realtime Robotics’ relationships with automotive original equipment manufacturers and their production ecosystems while pursuing opportunities in other complex manufacturing industries.

##### To free the world of dull and dangerous tasks.

Two robots with realtime robotics software on screen in background

## Our story

photo of the realtime robotics leadership team

### The spark.

In his early days at Duke, co-founder George Konidaris launched a project to take on a classic robotics challenge: developing a motion planning processor that can generate motion plans in real-time. It became clear his team had a real solution on their hands. Rather than just writing a paper, George wanted to make the solution a reality. He connected with fellow professor Dan Sorin, and together they founded Realtime Robotics.

A complex robotic automation system with multiple robotic arms and colourful components

### The revolution. [...] ## Our team

##### Meet the leadership

Peter Howard

##### Peter Howard

CEO [...] Peter Howard is the Chief Executive Officer of Realtime Robotics. He has a passion for innovative business formation, and the process of creating order and value out of formative chaos. His roles have included entrepreneur-CEO, investor, and board director. As CEO, Peter has founded and successfully grown four previous companies, leading two to IPOs, one to strategic sale, and another to a major technology license.

My third startup company was based on an amazing sensor technology that became a standard for measurement of large manufactured products like aircraft and automobiles. We worked with BMW to mount that sensor on robotic arms on their X5 line to monitor and correct dimensional problems they were having. We succeeded with the monitoring part of that, but making on-the-fly adjustments to robot programs in the line was deemed too risky. Fifteen years later, I got a call from Duke University about a breakthrough in robotic motion planning. I flew down, met the inventors, and saw something that could fundamentally change how robots could move and adapt safely. The importance of the breakthrough and the quality of the inventor team was enough. I put in the first funds and together we got the [...] The argument between the two ultra-wealthy titans is over a decade old, and Elon Musk’s Full Self Driving vehicle still can’t make it more than 20 minutes on New England roads without having to wrest control back to avoid a life-threatening event, and Mark Zuckerberg social media algorithms have nearly destroyed our ability to tell the difference between evidence-based facts and alternative facts of the sort that cause Boeing aircraft to fall from the sky and Tesla vehicles to commit murder-suicide.

Based on fact-based evidence, my position would have to be that the far more real and imminent risk is giving any unsupervised agency to any AI. [...] Peter Howard is the President and CEO of Realtime Robotics. As a CEO, Peter has founded and successfully grown five companies, leading two to IPOs, one to strategic sale, and another to a major technology license. Peter has led Realtime Robotics through several successful rounds of funding, was key in its product development and in helping the company land several contracts with global 100 firms.

Thank you so much for joining us in this interview series! Before we dive in, our readers would love to “get to know you” a bit better. Can you tell us a bit about your ‘backstory’ and how you got started in robotics?
